options: A. Use your home street address and birth year as your password across all websites so you never forget it, and accept friend requests from unknown adults.

C. Disable firewall and operating system security updates because patches slow down video streaming and gaming.
D. Click on urgent pop-up links claiming your account is suspended and enter your credentials on the linked form immediately.

requirements.lead_text: Do THREE of the following. For each project you complete, copy the files to a backup device and share the finished projects with your counselor.
requirements.req_text: Do THREE of the following. For each project you complete, copy the files to a backup device and share the finished projects with your counselor. (a) Using a spreadsheet or database program, develop a food budget for a patrol weekend campout OR create a troop roster that includes the name, rank, patrol, and telephone number of each Scout. Show your counselor that you can sort the roster by each of the following categories: rank, patrol, and alphabetically by name. (b) Using a word processor, write a draft letter inviting the parents or guardians of your troop's Scouts to a troop event. Resource: Word Processing Tutorial (video) (c) Using a graphics program, design and draw a campsite plan for your troop OR create a flyer for an upcoming troop event, incorporating text and some type of visual such as a photograph or an illustration. (d) Using a presentation software program, develop a report about a topic approved by your counselor. For your presentation, create at least five slides, with each one incorporating text and some type of visual such as a photograph or an illustration. (e) Using a digital device, take a picture of a troop activity. Send or transfer this image to a device where it can be shared with your counselor. (f) Make a digital recording of your voice, transfer the file to a different device, and have your counselor play back the recording. (g) Create a blog and use it as an online journal of your Scouting activities, including group discussions and meetings, campouts, and other events. Include at least five entries and two photographs or illustrations. Share your blog with your counselor. You need not post the blog to the internet; however, if you choose to go live with your blog, you must first share it with your parent or guardian AND counselor AND get their approval. (h) Create a webpage for your troop, patrol, school, or place of worship. Include at least three articles and two photographs or illustrations. Include at least one link to a website of interest to your audience. You need not post the page to the internet; however, if you decide to do so, you must first share the webpage with your parent or guardian AND counselor AND get their approval.

pamphlet_excerpts: Organizing Information With Databases: Database manager (DBM) programs are used for organizing, storing, and keeping track of a set of information called a database (p. 49).
Database Records and Fields: The data are organized in lines called records, with each record consisting of a number of fields (p. 49).
Uniform Field Structure Across Records: For each new record, the same set of fields is stored, with different contents in each field (p. 49).
Troop Attendance Database Design: A troop attendance database could be set up with a record for each Scout in the troop (p. 49).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Define Standard Database Fields: For each new record, the same set of fields is stored, with different contents in each field (p. 49).
Step 2 - Create Individual Scout Records: A troop attendance database could be set up with a record for each Scout in the troop (p. 49).
Step 3 - Add Patrol and Rank Columns: Each record would consist of fields for the Scout's name, patrol, rank, troop meeting attendance, campout attendance, and other events (p. 49).
Step 4 - Log Event Attendance Status: An entry of "present" or "absent" could be made in the appropriate field of each Scout's record after each activity (p. 49).

B. Lossless compression restores the exact original data without losing a single character or instruction
C. Lossy compression only works on computers built before 1990
D. Lossless compression automatically converts text files into MP3 audio
choices: A. Lossless compression permanently removes unimportant numbers to save space
B. Lossless compression restores the exact original data without losing a single character or instruction
C. Lossy compression only works on computers built before 1990
D. Lossless compression automatically converts text files into MP3 audio
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Lossless compression restores the exact original data without losing a single character or instruction
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Lossless compression reduces file size while preserving 100 percent of the original data, which is essential for text, spreadsheets, and executable programs where missing bytes would corrupt the file (p. 26).
